findings: F-1 (material, r7 template defect): authorization gate1 'git log --branches --not --remotes -- <path> empty' is UNREACHABLE in any repo with zero remote-tracking refs — every commit ever made is listed. Obsidian-class tickets are therefore impossible gate1-as-written in the live lane (dead origin). Amendment proven on fixture: when refs/remotes is empty, toolB VERIFIED(moved-to-obsidian) (both digests re-hash) substitutes for the unpushed-half.

F-2 (material, r7 template defect): authorization gate2 'status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- <path> empty' forbids every UNTRACKED candidate by definition ('?? <path>' always prints) — the stale class is unreachable as written; this is exactly how lore/.scratch-style candidates were auto-denied in r7. Amendment proven on fixture: gate2' = porcelain excluding untracked lines (tracked dirt only); untracked-ness is the ticket's own substance, re-checked by refs=0.

F-3 (calibration): tool receipts alone are NOT authorization — toolA emits SAFE(pushed) for a file with UNCOMMITTED worktree modifications (try_pushed never inspects the worktree). The r7 gate2 layer is what catches it. Keep gates AND tools in step_0_recheck.

F-4 (flow semantics): plain mv staging preserves mtime+basename, so a stale-class staged copy still verifies SAFE(stale) under the mangled path while pushed/obsidian-class staged copies verify NOT-SAFE. The staged copy carries NO independent authorization — the second check must gate on byte-identity + gate stability (as implemented), never on the staged copy's own receipt.

F-5 (close-out): quarantining a TRACKED path leaves an unstaged deletion (' D <path>') after step_4; untracked (stale-class) staging leaves the worktree clean. Runbook close-out: record the deletion receipt in LOG.md; the parent decides when the deletion is committed.

hardening_found_by_this_seat: The runner's own first draft used '[ cond ] && check' patterns that SILENTLY SKIP a check on failure — 3 audits and several flow checks were invisible. Converted every check to explicit if/else; the hardened run then surfaced 5 real defects (2 of them in the fixture semantics, 3 in audit self-matching). Lesson for the fleet: a check framework must count the checks that DID NOT fire; a green summary with a variable check count is not evidence.
